title: Patch: the Duos AI weighs the teammate's whole hand before it passes

**Issue #4932 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #4932: Patch: the Duos AI weighs the teammate's whole hand before it passes
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In Duos games against the AI team, the AI may pass a card to its teammate when its own turn ends. To decide, it scores what the teammate could do with the card and what the teammate's best play without it is. Both scores stop after 8 candidate plays, cut in engine list order, not by value. A teammate holding 9-10 cards (the hand cap is 10) therefore has some cards cut before anything is scored, so the AI can pass a card the teammate cannot use, or keep one the teammate needed, purely because the good play sat past the cut. Players see this as the AI team passing badly in long Duos games with full hands.

## Why

`pass_score` (`crates/ai/src/duos.rs:426-461`) chains the passed card's own plays first, then the teammate's other plays in `legal_actions` order, and takes `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` (8, `crates/ai/src/config.rs:133`); `mate_baseline` (`crates/ai/src/duos.rs:508-521`) takes the first `Play` of each of at most 8 hand cards. With `HAND_CAP` 10 (`crates/engine/src/config.rs:57`), a full teammate hand leaves two cards (and in `pass_score`, every play past the eighth) unweighed. Hand order is arrival order, not value order, so the cut is arbitrary: a removal or lethal sitting ninth in the list never enters either side of the comparison. No open issue covers this (#4795 is the pass nonce bug, a different mechanism), and none of the rejected suggestions does (#4533 is about the 1v1 reply spending Credits and trading dead Tradables). The node cost need not move: the same 8 engine steps, chosen better.

## Proposal

Order the teammate's candidate first-plays by a free static score (hand value) before taking the 8 in `pass_score` and `mate_baseline` (and the same card's variants in `own_use_gain`), so the bound keeps the best 8 instead of the first 8. Add scene tests with a 10-card teammate hand where the best follow-up sits past the old cut: the pass decision must match full-hand scoring. Screen on the Duos gate series with candidate and control builds on the same frozen seeds (same deals), keeping the change only on a paired comparison decided in advance that shows no regression and on scene tests carrying the behavior.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/duos.rs` (`pass_score`, `mate_baseline`, `own_use_gain` ordering; no new nodes)
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (comment on `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` recording the screen)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/duos.rs` (scene tests: full-hand pass choice with 9-10 cards)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scene test fails without the fix (pass differs from full-hand scoring when the best play is past the cut) and passes with it; a 10-card hand case and a below-the-bound case that is unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate --duos` smoke green with the candidate (no fallback, refusal or panic, which already fails the gate).
- [ ] Candidate-versus-control paired comparison on the same duos-gate seeds, size and keep bar decided in advance, shows no regression.
- [ ] Per-pass engine-step count unchanged (still at most 8 takes per scoring site) unless a measured raise is part of the kept change.

## Size and risks

Small (ordering plus tests); measurement is the duos gate plus a paired same-seed comparison, both cheap next to a 400-game screen. Risk is that static ordering mis-ranks versus engine-step scoring; contained because the max is still taken over real engine steps, only over a better 8, and the gate plus scene tests hold behavior.

---

## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45664712619)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

When the Duos AI decides whether to pass a card, its two scores read the teammate's best-valued cards, not the first cards in hand order. The scores are `pass_score` and `mate_baseline`. This holds at any hand size, because the hand cap is a setting (R1143, 0 to `HAND_CAP_MAX`) and nothing may assume 10. The engine-step bound stays at `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` (8) per scoring site. A hand that fits the bound scores exactly as before.

What the code does today:
- `mate_baseline` takes the first 8 distinct hand cards. A winning ninth card never enters the baseline, so a card the teammate cannot use better is passed. This is the bug that changes decisions.
- `pass_score` cuts by plays, not cards. A Unit lists one play per open lane, so 8 plays reach one or two cards. Its cut cannot flip a decision on its own, because the passed card's own plays come first. It gets the same rule because the issue asks for it and R1127000 would otherwise keep an arbitrary cut.

Decisions the issue did not settle:
- **Bound stays 8, not the hand size.** The maintainer's "should read an arbitrary value" is read as: tests and code must not hard-code 10, and ordering works at any hand length. The rejected alternative is lifting the bound to the hand size (up to 14 steps per site). That adds unmeasured cost and contradicts "no new nodes".
- **`own_use_gain` and `pass_gain`'s `card_plays` are untouched.** They hold variants of one card, which tie on hand value, so ordering them changes nothing. The judge flagged the same tie.
- **Ranking applies only on overflow.** A hand within the bound keeps its order, so existing behaviour and tie-breaks do not move.
- **Pairing method for the paired screen (decided now):** two builds of the same duos gate on the same frozen deals. Size is `--games 40`. Keep bar is below.
- **A ruling is needed.** R1127000 and R1723000 state the cut order, so a new note amends them.

2. **`crates/ai/src/duos.rs`: add a helper** next to `best_step`:
   ```rust
   /// R4932000: the plays that get scored, at most `limit`. A list that fits is kept as it came, in
   /// `legal_actions` order, so a hand within the bound scores as it always has. A longer one is cut to
   /// the first play of each card it names, the `limit` cards worth most first (`hand_card_value` on
   /// `state`, the teammate's probe), ties in the order they came; a play of a card outside the hand
   /// (a graveyard play, R454) ranks last. The bound is unchanged: no engine step is added.
   fn best_valued_plays(state: &GameState, mate: PlayerId, plays: Vec<ActionBody>, limit: usize) -> Vec<ActionBody> {
       if plays.len() <= limit {
           return plays;
       }
       let worth = |action: &ActionBody| match action {
           ActionBody::Play { instance_id, .. } => state.players[mate]
               .hand
               .iter()
               .find(|card| card.id == *instance_id)
               .map_or(f64::NEG_INFINITY, |card| hand_card_value(state, card, &AI_EVAL)),
           _ => f64::NEG_INFINITY,
       };
       let mut seen: IndexSet<String> = IndexSet::new();
       let mut ranked: Vec<(f64, ActionBody)> = plays
           .into_iter()
           .filter(|action| matches!(action, ActionBody::Play { instance_id, .. } if seen.insert(instance_id.clone())))
           .map(|action| (worth(&action), action))
           .collect();
       ranked.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal)); // stable
       ranked.into_iter().take(limit).map(|(_, action)| action).collect()
   }
   ```

   best_step(mate_probe, mate, plays).unwrap_or_else(|| /* unchanged fallback */)

- `use jackioh_engine::config::{HAND_CAP, HAND_CAP_MAX}` (extend the existing `jackioh_engine::config` import).
- `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` in the `jackioh_ai::{…}` list (the crate re-exports `config::*`).

Helper (reuses `winning_pass_state`, `set_hand`, `side`, `A1`, `A2`, `BIG`, `ONE_DROP`, `STAB`):
```rust
/// `winning_pass_state`'s round 1 (A1 at pass mana, A2 at BIG's mana, B2 at an effective life of 3),
/// A1 holding only BIG so it can play nothing, A2 with a hand cap of `cap` and `held` cards: one-drops,
/// the Stab last when `stab`. Returns the state and BIG's id.
fn crowded_mate_state(seed: &str, cap: i32, held: usize, stab: bool) -> (DuosState, String) {
    let (mut state, ..) = winning_pass_state(seed);
    let big = set_hand(&mut state, A1, &[BIG]).remove(0);
    side(&mut state, A2).hand_cap = Some(cap);
    let mut hand = vec![ONE_DROP; held - usize::from(stab)];
    if stab {
        hand.push(STAB);
    }
    set_hand(&mut state, A2, &hand);
    (state, big)
}
```

1. `r4932000_a_crowded_hand_is_weighed_by_its_best_cards_at_any_hand_cap`
   - Loop `cap` over `[HAND_CAP, HAND_CAP + 2, HAND_CAP_MAX]`.
   - Set `held = usize::try_from(cap - 1)`, so one slot is free.
   - Build `crowded = crowded_mate_state(seed, cap, held, true)`. Assert the A2 hand length is `held`, the Stab's index is at least `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS`, and A1 cannot play BIG (`plays_in(&crowded.duels[0], PlayerId::P1, &big).is_empty()`).
   - Positive control: with `bare = crowded_mate_state(seed, cap, held, false)`, `duos_passes(&bare, A1) == vec![bare_big]`.
   - Full-hand reference: `alone = crowded_mate_state(seed, cap, 1, true)` (the Stab alone, nothing cut). Assert `duos_passes(&alone, A1).is_empty()` (the Stab wins either way, so BIG is kept).
   - Assert `duos_passes(&crowded, A1) == duos_passes(&alone, A1)`, with `cap` in each message.
2. `r4932000_a_hand_the_bound_holds_whole_is_scored_as_before`
   - Use `held = DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` at `HAND_CAP`, Stab last, so it is the 8th and last card the bound reaches.
   - Assert the hand length and that the Stab is last. Assert `duos_passes` is empty and equals the `alone` reference.
   - This passes before and after the change. It documents the unchanged side (acceptance's below-the-bound case).

Commands:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai r4932000`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai duos::`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`
- `cargo jackioh gate --duos`
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`

## Done when

- [ ] Test 1 failed before step 2–4 and passes after. Test 2 passes. Both positive controls hold.
- [ ] `best_valued_plays` is used in `mate_baseline` and `pass_score` only. Each site still scores at most 8 plays (`pass_score` takes 8 in total with its own plays first). Nothing in the code or tests assumes a hand size of 10.
- [ ] R4932000 note, `spec/pending/4932.md`, the two note edits and the §13.7 sentence are in. `cargo jackioh spec check` is green.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, rustfmt, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo jackioh gate --duos` are green. The full harness list (workspace clippy, `catalog check`, `patches check`, workspace tests) is green.
- [ ] The paired screen ran against its stated bar, and the config comment holds only measured numbers (or the report says it was skipped, or that the bar failed).
- [ ] No new `#[allow]`, no skipped or weakened test, and no edit under the forbidden paths.

## Risks

- **Determinism and replay.** The helper uses a stable sort, no hash order and no RNG, and the step nonce label is unchanged. `at` in `duos-pass-score:{at}` now indexes the ranked list, but the nonce is only an idempotency key. #4795 (the pass nonce bug) is a separate mechanism, so do not touch it.
- **Hidden information.** The value is read from the teammate's probe, which the team shares (B29), and no opponent card is read. The existing `b29_…` and `r1127000_hidden…` tests cover it.
- **Static ranking can mis-rank.** The max is still over real engine steps, only over a better 8. The screen and the tests hold it.
- **Graveyard plays (R454).** They rank last on overflow, as they came last before.
- **`pass_score`'s change has no decision-level test.** No scene separates it without a synergy card, and the builder should not invent one. It shares the helper that test 1 exercises.
- **Cost.** At most 8 steps per site, as before. The helper adds one `hand_card_value` read per candidate card.

## Open questions

- Is "should read an arbitrary value" satisfied by order-independent ranking plus hand-cap-driven tests (this plan)? Or should the bound itself become the hand's size? That would weigh every card at up to `HAND_CAP_MAX` steps per site and would need its own measurement. A person can answer this after the first screen.
````

# Plan (sonnet, medium)

## Goal

When the Duos AI decides whether to pass a card, its two scores read the teammate's best-valued cards, not the first cards in hand order. The scores are `pass_score` and `mate_baseline`. This holds at any hand size, because the hand cap is a setting (R1143, 0 to `HAND_CAP_MAX`) and nothing may assume 10. The engine-step bound stays at `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` (8) per scoring site. A hand that fits the bound scores exactly as before.

What the code does today:
- `mate_baseline` takes the first 8 distinct hand cards. A winning ninth card never enters the baseline, so a card the teammate cannot use better is passed. This is the bug that changes decisions.
- `pass_score` cuts by plays, not cards. A Unit lists one play per open lane, so 8 plays reach one or two cards. Its cut cannot flip a decision on its own, because the passed card's own plays come first. It gets the same rule because the issue asks for it and R1127000 would otherwise keep an arbitrary cut.

Decisions the issue did not settle:
- **Bound stays 8, not the hand size.** The maintainer's "should read an arbitrary value" is read as: tests and code must not hard-code 10, and ordering works at any hand length. The rejected alternative is lifting the bound to the hand size (up to 14 steps per site). That adds unmeasured cost and contradicts "no new nodes".
